title: Prompt qualification record
description: The SPEC-024 qualification-registry record that a prompt-bearing model-execution route must carry (ADR-044). SPEC-027 places its reference on the adapter enablement record, never on the live-call authorization, so this record reaches a run transitively: prompt qualification -> enablement -> authorization. It binds the frozen prompt artifact's exact bytes to the stage-output contract, the execution and routing contracts, the governing qualification policy, and a tracked change request. No free-text property and no credential-shaped property: a governance chain must not become a channel for prose or for secret material. Two disjoint bases exist. `bootstrap_pre_evaluation` is the pre-evaluation shape used before any completed evaluation run exists; it can only ever authorize `live_dev`. `evaluated_comparison` is the post-evaluation shape, and it is UNREACHABLE in E-B: its `supporting_evaluation_references` resolve against an evaluation-artifact root that no runtime injects or hash-verifies yet, so the E-B v2 runtime refuses that basis outright rather than accept a schema-valid but unverified record. A successor increment introduces that third root together with the second property set. No schema file executes on the run path (ADR-032); every const, enum, and conditional here is re-enforced in `extraction.prompt_qualification`.

change_request_reference.description: Tracked under `evals/change_requests/` and therefore resolved against the injected repository root, never against the governance artifact root. The negative lookahead is not decoration: in ECMA-262 `$` matches before a trailing line terminator, so a plain anchored pattern would admit a reference carrying an embedded newline.

decided_at.description: A timezone-aware ISO-8601 instant. Awareness and chronology are enforced at runtime, where a naive timestamp is refused rather than assumed to be UTC.

declared_non_claims.description: Present only under `bootstrap_pre_evaluation`, where it states in closed vocabulary what the record does not assert. Forbidden under `evaluated_comparison`, whose whole purpose is that a release qualification may in fact be claimed. `prefixItems` plus `items: false` fixes the exact ordered tuple; an `enum` with `uniqueItems` would have admitted any permutation of the four values.

governing_spec_reference.description: A const, not a pattern. The policy that governs a prompt qualification record is the SPEC-024 qualification registry, whatever stage the prompt serves. A stage spec such as SPEC-008 is stage context and is cited by the tracked change request; naming it here would mislabel stage context as qualification policy.

known_limitation_codes.description: Closed vocabulary. Prose belongs in the tracked change request, which this record pins by reference and digest.

prompt_artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the exact bytes of the frozen prompt artifact, with no normalization. Equal by construction to `extraction.prompts.load_prompt(...)['prompt_hash']`, and compared to it at runtime, so a single edited byte breaks the chain and forces requalification.

qualification_status.description: `bootstrap_authorized_live_dev` is reachable only under `bootstrap_pre_evaluation`, and the evaluated branch excludes it; the two are bound by an exact iff.

review_decision.description: Present only under `evaluated_comparison`. `evals/CHANGE_CONTROL_PROTOCOL.md` states that a review decision presupposes a completed, valid evaluation, so a pre-evaluation record may not carry one at all -- not even an empty or neutral value.

supporting_evaluation_references.description: Present only under `evaluated_comparison`. These resolve against an evaluation-artifact root that is a distinct third root from the governance artifact root and the repository root. No runtime injects or hash-verifies that root yet, which is exactly why the evaluated basis is refused in E-B.
